intro_html: Massaman is the gentlest of the Thai curries and the one with the longest passport. It came into southern Thailand through Persian and Indian traders, which is why it carries potatoes and peanuts and a sweetness that the other curries do not have. It is thick, mild enough that kids will eat it, and it is basically a stew wearing a curry's clothes. Each serving lands at 668 calories and 30 grams of protein for about $2.34.
cost_closing_html: About $2.34 a serving. Coconut milk is the single largest line all by itself, bigger than the chicken, and it is not optional, because massaman without a proper coconut body is just potato soup with ambition.
shop_smart: Coconut milk is the dominant line here by a distance. Buy full fat store brand cans and buy them when they are on sale, since a stack of cans in the pantry keeps for a year and this recipe wants several.
Potatoes and carrots are what make this the cheapest-eating of the Thai curries, because they add real volume for pennies. Buy both by the bag rather than loose.
Peanut butter and chopped peanuts both go in, and one jar of each covers many batches. Buy the plain sixteen ounce jar rather than anything specialty.
Chicken breast is the largest single line. Thighs would cut that noticeably and would survive the long simmer better, so make the swap if the price matters more than the label.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Spoon the thick cream off the top of the unshaken coconut milk cans into your largest pot, keeping the thin liquid aside. Cook it with the olive oil over medium-high for 3 to 5 minutes until the oil separates.
Add the curry paste and the diced onion and fry them in that oil for 3 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens and smells toasted.
Add the chicken cut into chunks along with the garlic and grated ginger, and turn everything until coated.
Pour in the reserved coconut liquid, then add the cubed potatoes and sliced carrots. Bring it to a simmer.
Stir in the peanut butter, brown sugar and fish sauce, then simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes until the potatoes are fork tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened around them.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice, tasting as you go. Massaman should read sweet first, salty second and sour last, in that order.
Fold in most of the chopped peanuts and the cilantro, holding some of each back to scatter on top.
portion_html: Set the loaded pot on the scale, subtract the empty-pot weight, and divide by 14. Same amount in every container. Each one carries 668 calories, and the potatoes mean this holds its texture on reheat better than a rice-heavy bowl does.

head.description: Massaman chicken curry with potatoes, carrots and peanuts in a thick coconut sauce. Built as 14 meal prep servings at 668 calories, 30g protein, about $2.34 each.
head.keywords: massaman curry, thai chicken curry, coconut potato curry, peanut curry, thai meal prep, mild curry recipe
steps: Fry the thick coconut cream with oil until it splits, then fry the curry paste and onion 3 minutes.
Add the chunked chicken, garlic and ginger and coat in the paste.
Add the reserved coconut liquid, potatoes and carrots and bring to a simmer.
Stir in peanut butter, brown sugar and fish sauce and simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes until thick.
Finish with lime juice, chopped peanuts and cilantro, then portion into 14 containers.
